findings.evidence: `TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Curve/IntegralBound.lean` and `TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/ArcFTC.lean` are the existing precedent: raw-curve contour-integral lemmas living outside the winding layer with Mathlib-only imports (`public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.Basic` / `.FundThmCalculus`). The five declarations' statements reference only `deriv`, `HasDerivAt`, `ContinuousOn`, `Set.uIcc` and `intervalIntegral`.
findings.fix: Move those five declarations to a curve-level file, e.g. `TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Curve/Reparam.lean` (importing only `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.IntegrationByParts`), and keep `windingNumber_comp_reparam`, `windingNumber_comp_affine`, `IsNullHomologous.comp_reparam` in `Winding/Number/Reparam.lean`, importing the new file.
findings.issue: `hasDerivAt_comp_reparam`, `deriv_comp_reparam`, `uIcc_endpoints_subset_image`, `eqOn_deriv_comp_reparam` and `integral_deriv_smul_comp_reparam` mention no winding number and use only Mathlib; placing them under `Winding/Number/` forces any contour-integral consumer to import `NullHomologous` → `Winding/Number/Basic` → `Cauchy/PrincipalValue/Basic` to get a change-of-variables lemma for `∫ deriv γ • f ∘ γ`.

summary: The winding-number results are correctly placed in Winding/Number/, but the curve-level half of the file (chain rule, IVT containment, contour-integral change of variables) depends on no winding theory and is buried behind the principal-value/winding layer.
